Community assistance

Community Assistance & Practical Support

Mental health is affected by practical needs such as housing, food, transportation, safety, employment, childcare, and access to medical care. A resource guide should make those connections easier to find.

Last updated September 19, 2026 · Editorial policy

Types of help we are organizing

  • Food assistance and community meals
  • Housing and homelessness services
  • Utility and financial assistance
  • Transportation support
  • Family, parenting, and childcare resources
  • Disability and benefits navigation
  • Legal aid and victim services
  • Community clinics and low-cost medical care
Local directory in progress

Specific Treasure Valley organizations, eligibility rules, phone numbers, addresses, and hours will be added only after they are checked against current official sources.

A general starting point

In many U.S. communities, dialing 211 can connect people with local social-service information. Because local availability changes, verify current services and eligibility before relying on a listing.

Looking for local support?

Use the counselor directory to compare providers by specialty, approach, location, insurance, availability, and visit type.

About this guide: This page is educational and is not a diagnosis, treatment plan, or substitute for care from a qualified professional. If safety is an immediate concern, use the crisis resources on this site.

Need urgent help?

If there is immediate danger or a medical emergency, call 911. In the U.S., call or text 988 for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.
